articles.title: Popular Nintendo Blogger Supper Mario Broth Says He May Only Have a Year to Live
articles.summary: A popular Nintendo blogger who tells his viewers obscure facts about Super Mario has been hit with serious health conditions, including heart failure. The online personality has vowed to continue running the blog for as long as he’s able.
body: Supper Mario Broth is a blog and series of social media accounts known for posting arcane and funny trivia about everyone’s favorite Italian plumber. The blog has shared thousands of facts from the series since its creation in 2012.

“I am scared I will soon not be able to see Mario again,” he said in a post to his 270,000 X / Twitter followers. “However, I promise that until that day arrives, I will always be here, posting Mario facts. Thank you all so much for your support through the years.”
Despite a healthy lifestyle, the condition is genetic. According to the blogger, there’s a two-in-three chance he survives past one year.
The condition is also affecting his eyesight, degrading it over time. He isn’t sure whether surgery or medication can stop or slow this process yet.

articles.title: Mass Effect Creator Is ‘Optimistic’ the Series Will Live On
articles.summary: BioWare's shutdown has been one of the hardest studio closures in gaming history. The Edmonton-based studio made its way into thousands of gamers' hearts, and it was set to continue this mission with the development of Mass Effect Universe, the next entry in the Mass Effect series.
body: In 2020, in celebration of N7 Day, the annual celebration of the Mass Effect franchise, BioWare announced that it was working on a new Mass Effect game, but it was only in the early stages of development. Besides a handful of teasers, not much was heard about the project from then on. When private investors bought EA, Mass Effect 5 seemed increasingly unlikely. Unfortunately, that proved true: EA shut down BioWare and canceled the project on Oct. 21, 2026, nearly six years after its announcement.

However, neither fans nor developers were ready to give up on Mass Effect just yet. Petitions were created, billboards were put up to raise awareness, voice actors showed support, and developers even leaked an early trailer to fuel the fire. The community has come together, celebrating N7 Day in a uniquely special way.
points: BioWare's shutdown has been one of the hardest studio closures in gaming history.

articles.title: Dungeons in World of Warcraft: Forever get a huge XP buff, but power-levellers shouldn't celebrate just yet
articles.summary: World of Warcraft: Forever has received a massive buff to the XP drop-rates of dungeon mobs (enemies), which should make running these instances multiple times feel more rewarding - and may revive an older levelling strategy.
body: This buff is a 50 percent increase in experience from all mobs killed inside all dungeons. As detailed in this World of Warcraft forum post, community manager Kaivax wrote that this change has been made "so it feels better to go back in for more runs". They don't outright say this is in response to community feedback, but the subject has been a hot topic since the beta.

World of Warcraft: Forever developers have spoken in the past about the decision to deliberately bring down dungeon mob XP to disincentivise power-levelling in dungeons. The idea was that by doing this, people would be encouraged to actually go out into the world and explore it, rather than hopping from instance to instance until they reached max level.

Sadly, a side effect of this change is that doing a dungeon more than once could feel unrewarding. Playing it once is great, as you get to complete lots of quests that reward guaranteed items and XP. However, if you go back again, you don't get these, so your only source of progression comes from a heavily decreased XP rate.

articles.title: WoW: Forever Boosts Dungeon XP As Blizzard Struggles to Get Leveling Balance Right
articles.summary: Blizzard just gave some ground in its battle to get players to slow down and spend more time in the open world in World of Warcraft: Forever.
body: The developer applied a hotfix on Sunday that boosted experience points (XP) for killing monsters in dungeons by 50%. It's Blizzard's first concession to complaints from players that dungeons, a core part of the WoW experience, had become too unrewarding to play compared to questing in the open world.

Blizzard is struggling to find the sweet spot for leveling in WoW: Forever. The intention is that leveling in Forever should be faster and smoother than it was in classic WoW (which is definitely the case), but that the journey to level 60 should still feel substantial. Additionally, Blizzard is keen to promote the open-world questing experience and avoid players spending all their time running dungeons just to race to the finish line.

When the beta began, XP from killing monsters in dungeons was heavily reduced compared to WoW Classic, while XP for completing dungeon quests was dramatically increased — the idea being that dungeons would be worth running once, but after that, you'd return to questing.
points: Blizzard just gave some ground in its battle to get players to slow down and spend more time in the open world in World of Warcraft: Forever.

articles.title: Fortnite Officially Reveals Pirate Shop Access Token Odds
articles.summary: Since Fortnite Treasure Hunters began on Nov. 1, Epic Games has been flooded with disgruntled fans wanting to know the odds of treasures that can be found in chests this season, namely the Pirate Shop Access token.
body: The Pirate Shop Access token led fans to focus on opening chests rather than enjoying the highly-anticipated One Piece -themed season. After opening thousands of chests with no luck, fans wanted to know their chances of finding it. On Saturday, before Treasure Hours began, they spammed the hashtag ReleaseTheOdds, demanding Epic Games share the odds of each treasure in Fortnite. It finally complied.

According to Epic Games, the Pirate Shop Access token has a drop chance of 1 per 137,500 chests, which is the equivalent of 0.000007273%. Odds have not been tweaked throughout the season except for Treasure Hours timed-event — they were boosted 1.5x for the first Treasure Hour on Saturday, and 2x the second time around. The golden skin, which will rotate each week, is the rarest treasure players can find by far (1 per 1,562,500 chests), but it's safe to say that the token is still more desirable because it's worth the equivalent of thousands of dollars.

articles.title: Father Arrested After Leaving Sleeping 6-Year-Old Daughter in Line for Pokémon Cards
articles.summary: A South Carolina man has been arrested and accused of leaving his 6-year-old daughter asleep outside a Target store overnight to hold his place in line for Pokémon cards, it has been reported.
body: According to the Washington Post, John-Michael Dooley, 35, had been waiting with his daughter outside the store this past Friday in Charleston's West Ashley district, where a throng of Pokémon fans had slowly gathered overnight in anticipation of a newly released set of the popular trading cards.

A news release from the Charleston Police Department states that officers arrived at the store around 2:30am after receiving reports of an unattended child. Witnesses at the scene told police that Dooley handed his daughter a blanket and a pillow sometime after 1am, before leaving her asleep in his spot in line. Wheen Dooley failed to return after an hour, these concerned witnesses were forced to contact the authorities.

Eventually Dooley returned to the store and was promptly arrested. In an interview with authorities, he admitted to police that he had gone home and left his young daughter unattended so that he could hold his spot in the line, according to the Charleston Police.
Dooley was then charged with unlawful conduct toward a child. Police said that the girl was unharmed and immediately placed into emergency protective custody.

articles.title: Spy x Family Officially Announces New Season and Movie Coming Soon
articles.summary: One of the best anime series in recent years is coming with a new season and a feature film. Spy x Family, the comedy-action manga created by Tatsuya Endo and published by Shueisha, is getting a fourth anime season and a new movie, both coming in 2027.
body: The announcement, shared on Oct. 8 at the Spy x Family Anime Extra Mission II special event and on the official Spy x Family website, came as a pleasant surprise for fans. Season 3 of the anime aired from October to December 2025, exactly two years after season 2 ended. If the timeframe remains consistent, fans can expect season 4 to air at the end of 2027. The franchise's second movie will come out in the same year, following the success of Spy x Family's first outing in cinemas, Spy x Family Code: White, released in 2023.

The series' comedy stems from three people living together while hiding their true identities. Airheaded Anya is one of the most adorable characters in anime, while Loid and Yor's marriage of convenience is slowly (too slowly!) developing into a real romance. Seeing this dynamic built on lies grow into a real found family is truly heartwarming, but Spy x Family hides a much more serious side. The themes of war and violence are never treated dismissively, and the series has delivered some of the best reflections on the topic seen in the medium.

articles.title: U2's The Edge Apparently Wrote a Full Script for Elf 2 But Was Never Able to Bring It to Life
articles.summary: U2 guitarist The Edge apparently had such a good idea for Elf 2 that he went out of his way to write his own script. That's according to Elf actor and Dancing with the Stars legend Andy Richter, who spilled the beans about the musician's fondness for Christmas during an episode of The Daily Beast's…
body: Richter said the story of The Edge (real name: David Howell Evans) and his secret Elf 2 script comes from producer and frequent Will Ferrell collaborator Shauna Robertson. When exactly the elusive script would have been written is unclear.

"She was in Europe, and somebody reached out to her and said, 'The Edge from U2 has written a sequel to Elf, and he wants to talk to you about it.' It's the weirdest story, but apparently, it was fully written," Richter recalled. "Somewhere in the world, there is an Edge-penned Elf 2 out there, which I would love for that to make the light of day."

If you're unfamiliar with the guitarist or the group he's helped define for the last 50 years, U2 is the Irish rock band behind megahits like With Or Without You, I Still Haven't Found What I'm Looking For, Sunday Bloody Sunday, Where The Streets Have No Name, and more. He's a legendary guitar player behind a long list of instantly recognizable songs, and by comparison he's got little to no experience in the movie world.

articles.title: GTA 6 reportedly has 55 Achievements/Trophies, more than both GTA 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2 had at launch
articles.summary: GTA 6 is due to release on the 19th November on PS5, and Xbox Series X/S, and ahead of the highly-anticipated launch of Rockstar's latest sandbox adventure, people just can't get enough information about the game.
body: In a now-deleted tweet from (in)famous Rockstar dataminer, TexFunz2 - re-posted by the Twitter account iGrandTheftAuto - it appears the game will have 55 individual rewards for completing certain tasks and missions. At the time of writing, we don't know specifically what these challenges are, but it seems none of them will be attached to the online version of the game; the base game launches without GTA Online, and so we can safely assume that all these rewards will be for the single-player only content. GTA Online will drop sometime in 2027, according to Twitch's CEO.

If you've been paying attention to previous Rockstar titles, you'll know that Grand Theft Auto 5 launched with 51 Achievements/Trophies - again, all single-player - and Red Dead Redemption 2 launched with 52. So the latest game has more than either game got at launch - and I can tell you from experience, getting Platinum in either title was a very time-consuming experience. Expect the same to be true here, too.

articles.title: COD: Modern Warfare 4 gets a surprisingly sudden free trial, so you can see what the game's extraction mode DMZ is like
articles.summary: Activision has released the first trial for Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's extraction mode DMZ. The trial is available across PC (Steam / Battlenet), PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S until Wednesday, 11th November.
body: The free trial only includes access to DMZ and no other part of Modern Warfare 4, such as multiplayer or the campaign. And while it's not uncommon for Call of Duty titles to make some of their modes available for free for a limited time, the timing of this DMZ taster is notable.

DMZ launched days before Modern Warfare 4's 23rd October release date, meaning this first trial has arrived just two weeks after the game's full launch. By comparison, Black Ops 7's Endgame mode had its first free trial months after launch, in the game's third season. That said, Endgame continued to be freely available until Season 6.

The DMZ trial also coincides with the launch of Modern Warfare 4's iteration of free-to-play Call of Duty battle royale mode Warzone, and Season 1. Indeed, both DMZ and the new Warzone take place on the same Hajin map, so even if you don't decide to buy the full game to continue playing DMZ, some of that map knowledge will certainly transfer to Warzone.

articles.title: Denis Villeneuve Praises Human Creativity Over AI Prompts, Almost Announces New Bond
articles.summary: Denis Villeneuve has praised human creativity over AI prompts, and playfully stirred the pot over the increasing rumours and speculation surrounding the casting of the main character in his upcoming James Bond film.
body: Addressing the crowd at Saturday night's Art+Film fundraiser at the LACMA museum in Los Angeles where he was being honored for his contributions to cinema (thanks, THR ), the Dune: Part Three director took the opportunity to praise his heroes including Steven Spielberg and James Cameron, before speaking to the existential crisis currently being suffered by artists as a result of the rise of artificial intelligence.

"At the heart of every one of my films, there’s a question I need to answer," said Villeneuve. "The audience may see it or they may not, and that is fine. For me, each film is a statement to the unknown to try and find that answer. Perhaps those questions are more urgent now than ever."

"We are at the crossroad, asking what defines a human being and what human expression is worth? Every parent on Earth is a little worried about the world of our children will inherit. That question is at the heart of Dune: Part Three with Paul and Chani fighting to give their children a better world than the one they were given.”
The director went on to discuss the vital role that human creativity plays in the process of creating art.

articles.title: World of Warcraft: Forever bumps dungeon XP from monsters by 50% after some community feedback I will diplomatically call passionate
articles.summary: World of Warcraft: Forever made some changes to how dungeons work—rather than getting a bunch of XP from enemies in dungeons, you predominantly get experience points from the quests surrounding them.
body: Which is made slightly better for the fact that there are just more dungeons overall —so while you can't sit in dungeons until level 60, you can chain between those dungeons with minimal questing, though some questing is still basically mandatory if you care about being efficient.

This has been a point of consternation. Any brief visit over to the r/classicwow subreddit leads to a raft of complaint threads about dungeon XP, though other communities do vary. It should be mentioned that a singular subreddit isn't reflective of the game's entire population, mind—but it is notable how upset the dungeon-loving slice of WoW's playerbase is.

To try and soothe that ache, Blizzard's gone ahead and buffed the XP gain: "At about 11:05 PST today, we deployed a hotfix that increased kill experience in dungeons by 50%, so it feels better to go back in for more runs," writes community manager Kaivax. "Happy dungeon crawling, and good luck with those Deviate Hides!"
That 50% number isn't actually too much, mind—it's a 50% increase to the current value. So let's say you were getting 40 XP from a mob: You're now getting 60.
points: World of Warcraft: Forever made some changes to how dungeons work—rather than getting a bunch of XP from enemies in dungeons, you predominantly get experience points from the quests surrounding them.

articles.title: EVE Online's new expansion looks to make it simpler than ever to get into a huge space battle: 'Every 10 weeks or so, you're gonna know: I can roll up with whatever I have and go shoot some structures and have a big fight'
articles.summary: EVE Online is about to have a big week, with the introduction of paid, 24/7 alpha access to companion FPS Vanguard, as well as a new expansion for the OG MMO, Fractured Skies. Both are launching tomorrow, November 10.
body: That expansion is bringing a bunch of new features⁠—updated HUD, new ships, and further tweaks to the new player experience added over the summer⁠—but when I spoke with EVE design director Greg Hennessey, he was most excited about coming changes to lowsec PvP, and what they'll offer both new and experienced players.

EVE is most famous for the big intrigues and betrayals of nullsec space, but Hennessey estimated that participants in the more structured, constant lowsec conflicts "are actually probably our strongest PVP players in general.

"Our nullsec players are the ones who want to plot for three years and go have a billion dollar war for a year. [Lowsec] players every day are like, let's go out and brawl. Let's just go lose some ships, boys. Let's get out there."

Hennessey characterized Fractured Skies as the "second in a trilogy of expansions" overhauling faction conflict in lowsec. The summer expansion, Cradle of War, added ongoing Military Campaigns players could pitch in with to affect an ongoing story. Fractured Skies will introduce a recurring climax to factional PvP, with the first such Conquest scheduled for February.

articles.title: MSI Maestro 900R PC case review
articles.summary: The Maestro is a monstrous PC chassis with premium pretentions it just fails to grasp.
body: In short, I think you need to be someone who has their own staff.

That's partly a dig at its sheer scale—this thing is chomk with a capital CHOMK—but also at the fact only the very wealthy are going to consider this chassis a worthwhile casing for their gaming PC. This is a $700 (£800) PC case and that feels, on one hand, par for the course in these days of hyper-expensive everything, but also faintly anachronistic.

As always with the case reviewing process, I built a new PC inside it, and it only felt right to be doing so with high-end gear. So, I picked from the review kit that was in the cupboard: a MSI Godlike X with a Ryzen 9 9950X3D seemed appropriate, along with some 64 GB of G.Skill ULL memory and an RTX 5090. And that's when this whole endeavour started to feel like something from a bygone age.

videos.summary: The first half of NTE V1.5 "Once Upon a Glitched Call" is coming soon with the new character Elyms, plus new vehicles and gameplay!
body: Describe ETD-6’s lieutenant in a few words. There’s probably not a soul at the Bureau who doesn’t know her, right? "Understanding", "easygoing", "cheerful", "mischievous", "approachable", "polite to a fault", "witty", "kind"... Bureau staff rattled off adjective after adjective, every one of them a trait that makes a person easy to like. Sure, a few of those words seem to clash a little. But it’s perfectly natural for different people to see someone slightly differently, so don’t think too hard about it. On one point, at least, everyone agreed without a shred of doubt: "my friend."
points: The first half of NTE V1.5 "Once Upon a Glitched Call" is coming soon with the new character Elyms, plus new vehicles and gameplay!
